text:
maya: Hey all, trying to run the local dev stack on my new M1 mac. docker-compose up shows postgres container restarting. App (on host) says "could not connect to server". Compose snippet: 

maya: ```
services:
  postgres:
    image: postgres:14
    volumes:
      - ./data/postgres:/var/lib/postgresql/data
    ports:
      - "5432:5432"
```

alex.devx: Welcome! First quick checks: `docker-compose logs postgres` and whether the container fails due to permission/arch. On mac, bind mounts often hit permission issues.

maya: logs show `could not change permissions of /var/lib/postgresql/data: Permission denied` and container restarts.

trent.infra: Yep that's the classic bind-mount problem. Two options: 1) chown the host dir to postgres uid `sudo chown -R 999:999 ./data/postgres` then recreate the container, or 2) use a named volume to avoid host FS perms: `volumes: - pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data` and add `volumes:
  pgdata:` at the bottom. Named volumes are friendlier on mac.

maya: Tried chown, container starts and now `database system is ready to accept connections` shows in logs. But my Rails app still failed until I set `PGHOST=127.0.0.1` — it was trying sockets.

alex.devx: Right — when app runs on host use 127.0.0.1 and ensure ports are mapped. If app is in a container, use service name `postgres` as host.

maya: Also had Redis give ECONNREFUSED. Fixed by exposing 6379 and setting `REDIS_URL=redis://127.0.0.1:6379/1`.

infra-bot: [notice] postgres restarted 2 times in last 10m (container postgres).

trent.infra: If you see architecture warning on M1, prefer images that support arm64 (postgres:14 is usually fine). If you want, use the repo's `local-stack.yml` template which uses named volumes and correct hosts. Ping me and I'll share it.

maya: Thanks! Saved my morning. Happy to be here :)
